newsitem.title: THAILAND: IMF's Camdessus sees Thai economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus sees Thai economic recovery.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday that Thailand's economy should improve soon with export growth picking up and the current account deficit being curbed by the new government.

Camdessus told reporters after a meeting with newly-appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan that he believed new government initiatives explained to him could put the country back on track.
"I must tell you that the presentation that (Amnuay) made to me of his intention reassures me because it truly seems to be what is needed," he said.
Camdessus was on a day-long visit to Thailand at Amnuay's invitation after attending the World Trade Organization meeting in Singapore.

He said Thailand's current account deficit was too high and suggested a rebalancing of savings and investment. He said he agreed with a government plan to use more fiscal policy to manage the country's economy rather than rely heavily on monetary policies alone.

The concerns over the current account gap, which is expected to widen up to 8.3 percent of gross domestic product year, had been heightened in recent months because of political uncertainties, sluggish exports and volatile short-term inflows, he said.

Amnuay represents the new Thai government led by premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh which came into power earlier this month after November 17 polls. The new government has pledged to boost the slowing Thai economy projected by private analysts to grow by just more than six percent after a decade of nearly nine percent growth until 1995.
